global_items.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
global_items.summary: A global map categorizing every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into distinct forest types.
global_items.articleText: October 22, 2026 Research Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton Read the paper Share A new 10-meter resolution map shows which of the world's forests are natural, planted, or farmed, and how they are changing over time Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms. Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research, together with the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), are releasing Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 , a global map that categorizes every 10-by-10-meter patch of land on Earth into six distinct forest and land-use types, a key baseline for the EU's deforestation regulation. Alongside it, we're sharing an early time series that tracks how these forests changed each year from 2017 to 2025, including where natural forests were replaced by plantations or farms. For the first time, users can see at 10-meter detail worldwide, year by year, not just where forest was lost, but what replaced it: a timber plantation, a tree-crop farm or other land. Why "tree cover" isn't enough All forests store carbon and, together, forests are home to most of the world's land-based plant and animal species. But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history: a primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation that is harvested every decade or two. Most global maps only indicate whether trees are present. That's a challenge for those trying to protect natural forests. The European Union's regulation on deforestation-free products (EUDR), for example, requires that products like coffee, cocoa or palm oil do not originate from land that was forest in 2020 and has since been converted to agriculture. Similarly, wood products, such as furniture, must also be free of forest degradation: they can't come from primary forests that have since been converted into plantation or planted forests, or from naturally regenerating forests that have since been converted into plantation forests. As a result, companies and regulators need to know not just where trees are, but what kind of forest they form (primary or regrowing, planted or plantation, forest or farm) and what replaces that forest after a harvest. Last year, we jointly released Natural Forests of the World 2020 , a 10-meter resolution global map that separated natural forests from all other tree cover. It offered a starting point to help companies and regulators implement the EU Deforestation Regulation, and to support commodity producers in meeting their commitments not to convert natural forest. That map answered one question for every patch of land: was it natural forest in 2020 or not? ForTy goes further, showing what kind of forest is there, from primary forest to timber plantation to tree crops, and, with the new time series, how that changes each year. How ForTy classifies the world's forests Specifically, ForTy sorts land into six categories based on definitions from the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO): Primary forest: native forest with no visible signs of human disturbance. Naturally regenerating forest: forest that grew back on its own, for example after logging or fire. Planted forest: forest that people planted or seeded, and managed over long cycles. Plantation forest: fast-growing, intensively managed tree farms, often of one species. Tree crops and agroforestry: farms that grow things other than wood, like oil palm, rubber, cocoa, or fruit. Other land: everything else, from grassland and cropland to cities and water. The Forest Typology map for 2020. Each color shows the most common forest or land type in each square kilometer. Explore it at 10-meter detail in our Earth Engine app . Training our ForTy model was challenging because these categories depend in part on how land is used, not just how it looks. To teach our model the difference, we built a large-scale collection of forest-type examples with about 1.7 million labeled locations drawn from expert surveys, national and regional datasets, and targeted reviews of places where the model struggled. The model uses a custom architecture designed for the challenges of remote sensing data, and takes as a key input AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings , data-compact summaries of years of satellite observations for each 10-meter pixel, so it can spot subtle clues like planting patterns, growth cycles and harvest rhythms. From above, the five forest and tree-crop classes can look alike. ForTy is able to identify the subtle differences in structure and seasonal patterns that set them apart, accurately categorizing them in a global map database. Imagery © Google Earth, Maxar Technologies, Airbus. Putting the map to the test A map is only useful if people can trust it. So, with IIASA and WRI, we validated ForTy against more than 9,000 randomly chosen sites around the world. At each site, two trained experts studied high-resolution imagery and years of satellite records to determine which type of land was really there. ForTy picked the right forest type 90% of the time, and told forest apart from non-forest land 95% of the time, outperforming other global forest maps. Beyond accuracy, we know that global conservation is not one-size-fits-all. Instead of giving a yes-or-no label for a specific patch of land, ForTy provides a probability score for each class, enabling users to adapt the classification to regional contexts and application-specific precision trade-offs. For example, a company assessing deforestation risk under EUDR might set a strict threshold, only accepting pixels the model is highly certain about to avoid regulatory risks. Meanwhile, a researcher estimating total forest extent might use the full spectrum of probabilities to get a fuller picture of the potential landscape. From a single snapshot in time to a story of change A map of a single year is a useful baseline, but forests change. Our new early-release time series applies a similar approach to every year from 2017 to 2025. It shows not only where forests disappear and where they grow back, but also what kind of change happened: a natural forest turned into a timber plantation, for example, or abandoned land slowly regenerating into forest. This differentiation matters because some of the most important changes are hard to see from space. When a natural forest is logged and replanted as a plantation, the land soon looks green again, so standard tree-cover maps might not pick up the change. ForTy's time series makes these hidden changes visible, both losses and gains. Your browser does not support the video tag. What's next The Forest Typology 2020 map [described in Scientific Data] and the new time series are now freely available on Google Earth Engine under an open license. We hope governments, companies, conservation groups and scientists will use them to help build deforestation-free supply chains, direct forest finance where it’s needed, and protect the natural forests that matter most. Over the coming months, we'll keep improving the time series with our partners and users, and we'd love to hear how you use it. ForTy is part of our portfolio of research on AI for Nature , which includes mapping the drivers of forest loss, forecasting deforestation risk, modelling global species distributions, and monitoring biodiversity in the field. FortTy is also the latest addition to Google Earth AI , Google’s collection of geospatial models and datasets designed to help tackle the planet's most critical environmental challenges. We'd like to thank our co-authors Anton Raichuk, Peter Potapov, Myroslava Lesiv, Matthew Overlan, Mélanie Rey, Ravindran Rajakumar, Michelangelo Conserva, Radost Stanimirova, Michelle Sims, Sarah Carter, Elizabeth Goldman, Yuchang Jiang, Linus Scheibenreif, Ivelina Georgieva, Maria Shchepashchenko, Steffen Fritz, Nicholas Clinton, Dan Morris and Drew Purves, as well as the trusted testers who helped improved the map. global_items.title: Dream Labs raises $90M and launches Dream API
global_items.summary: Dream Labs says its Dream-1 AI model works across robots from different manufacturers and will allow robots to transfer their learning. The post Dream Labs raises $90M and launches Dream API appeared first on The Robot Report .
global_items.articleText: Dream Labs said its models learn how the physical world works from video and can control new robots without any data. | Source: Dream Labs More brains are coming for robots. Dream Labs this week said it has raised $90 million in seed funding. The company also launched Dream API, a publicly available application programming interface to turn a robot’s camera feed and a plain-English instructions into motor commands, even for robots it has never seen before. Factories worldwide run a record 5 million industrial robots, yet nearly every one is programmed for a single task, and most cannot transfer what they have learned to other machines, noted Dream Labs. Low-cost robots now sell for a few thousand dollars but ship with no built-in intelligence. Teaching one robot one task can take specialists months, and a new task or new hardware often means starting from zero, according to the San Francisco startup. Dream Labs said its Dream-1 flagship model works across robots from different manufacturers. Trained on video of people performing everyday tasks, it can predict what will happen next and determine the robot’s resulting action. Because it learns from video rather than from a single machine, its capabilities transfer across hardware, Dream Labs claimed. The company said Dream-1 can control any robot “out of the box” with grippers and zero-shot learning. “The hardware is ready. What’s been missing is a brain any robot can use,” stated Joel Jang, co-founder and CEO of Dream Labs. “When you get into a rental car, you don’t relearn how to drive. You find the controls, and your past driving experience does the rest.” “Dream-1 approaches a new robot the same way, so a new robot can do useful work in minutes, not months,” he added. “And instead of edited demos, we’re giving people a working model they can test themselves, mistakes included.” B Capital and Kindred Ventures led the round. It also included participation from A.Capital, Unusual Ventures, SV Angel, Wing VC, Scribble VC, and Adrian Aoun, among others. Inside Dream Labs’ product portfolio Developers and robot enthusiasts can start using Dream Labs’ AI products today. The company said Dream API translates visual inputs and natural language prompts directly into robot actions. Developers can sign up, connect any robots with grippers, and the robot will carry out the task. Dream Labs runs its models in data centers around the world, so robots respond quickly wherever they are. The company also offers fine-tuning as a service. For unsupported hardware or new capabilities, developers and robot makers can submit a small batch of demonstration data to receive a tailored model within hours. Developers also have access to Dream Labs’ robot playground. Anyone with a browser can type commands to a robot in Dream Labs’ San Francisco office and watch it respond live and unedited, no robot purchase required. “A capable robot arm has gone from the price of a luxury car to the price of a high-end laptop. What it needs now is intelligence,” said Daisy Cai, general partner at B Capital. “This team did some of the defining work in robot learning at NVIDIA . Now anyone with an API key can build on it.” https://www.therobotreport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/launch.mp4 Startup works with more than 20 hardware partners Dream Labs supports robots today that cost between about $2,000 and $10,000. Dream-1 needs no extra data to control a two-armed robot with parallel grippers. For its over 20 hardware partners, Dream Labs said it goes beyond that baseline, refining the model for each robot so it performs at its best. Dream-1 currently handles tabletop tasks such as picking and placing objects and folding laundry, with support for wheeled mobile robots and dexterous hands to follow. The company said it plans use the new funding primarily for compute as it expands the tasks and robots Dream-1 can handle, and scales to support more users. “Our customers buy our robots to build things, and the hardest part has always been getting them to do actual work,” said Ryan Chan, co-founder and CEO of MakerMods, which sells $2,000 bimanual robot arms. “With Dream-1, our robot was up and running in a few minutes and attempting tasks we never programmed. We can focus on building better hardware, and our customers get intelligence that keeps improving.” Register now and help us celebrate 20 years of RoboBusiness! Tell Us What You Think! global_items.title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
global_items.summary: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA, powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF […]
global_items.articleText: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. RavenPack built a dataset generation pipeline on Bigdata.com that takes a plain-language research hypothesis and returns a labeled, backtest-ready dataset — running on a fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron model. Investors can use these datasets to identify, analyze and visualize market trends. Speeding Data Pipelines to Improve Fraud Detection RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs and NVIDIA cuDF help accelerate data processing across multi-terabyte-scale, siloed, regulated sources, compressing the time from data to decision for fraud and other scenarios. HSBC provides near-real-time client insights that support customer processes and on-demand decision-making while minimizing risk and fraud, powered by 5x faster data processing on Starburst Enterprise’s GPU Engine . Stripe , a global provider of programmable financial services, sees 42x faster data pipelines and 92% cost savings for its Stripe Radar fraud-detection platform with NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Ray Data in offline testing. This enables Stripe Radar’s machine learning pipelines to continuously optimize model training and improve fraud detection. Learn more about NVIDIA accelerated computing in financial services . See notice regarding software product information. global_items.title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
global_items.summary: To help developers rapidly build world models, which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open […]
global_items.articleText: To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANYbotics-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. Train, Adapt and Optimize Models With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended Cosmos Framework training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T , Alpamayo , QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. Cosmos Framework is an open, modular framework of model training and optimization tools and skills to accelerate world model development. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. Test Policies and Run Models Faster Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing. Multiview and multisensory video data generation for evaluating policies in closed loop simulation. Developers can deploy core Cosmos models using updated NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices, which deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations, while continuous video analysis enables sub-second alerts. For vision AI developers, the new NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) 3.3 , built on Cosmos NIM microservices, turns one prompt into an efficient video AI application and helps teams monitor 40% more video streams with the same GPU. ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform , built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint , to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, Fogsphere also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ADNOC-Cosmos.mp4 The Cosmos platform is fully modular and open. Developers can use Cosmos Data Factory to generate training datasets, Cosmos Framework to train and adapt world models, then deploy supported Cosmos models through NIM microservices . entries.title: MCP Servers v2.0.0 릴리스: 최신 프로토콜 지원 및 서버 구조 리팩터링

entries.title: PyPI에 배포된 LiteLLM 1.107.0 버전 악성코드 삽입 공급망 침해 사고
entries.reason: 널리 쓰이는 LLM 게이트웨이 라이브러리의 PyPI 배포판이 백도어 및 자격증명 탈취기에 오염된 사건으로, 보안 점검이 필수적입니다.

facts.statement: PyPI에 업로드되었던 LiteLLM 1.107.0 배포본 휠 파일에 자격증명 탈취기(cook.py)와 백도어 데몬(sitecustomize.py)이 포함되었으며, 이후 PyPI에서 제거되었습니다.
facts.quote: The LiteLLM 1.107.0 release on PyPI carries a credential stealer and a remote code execution backdoor.

facts.statement: 업스트림 GitHub 소스 트리에는 해당 악성 파일이 없었으며, 1.106.2 및 RC 릴리스들은 안전한 것으로 확인되었습니다.
facts.quote: The upstream GitHub source does not contain them. PyPI has since removed the release. Versions 1.106.2, 1.107.0rc1, and 1.107.0rc2 are clean.

draft.one_sentence_summary: Swift 기반 네이티브 ROS 2 지원 및 LeRobot 차이 분석 CLI 공개와 함께 추론 엔진·검색 API·오픈소스 모델 확장이 이어졌습니다.
draft.section_robotics:
- **Swift-ros2 3.0**: 별도의 브리지나 rcl 크로스 컴파일 없이 Zenoh 또는 DDS를 통해 Swift 앱이 ROS 2 그래프에 직접 참여하도록 지원하며, swift-ros2-rosidl 등 세 패키지로 분리되어 독립 GitHub 조직으로 이전되었습니다 [19].
- **robot-data-diff**: LeRobot 데이터셋의 두 리비전을 비교하여 에피소드 변경 내역과 액션 통계 및 유휴 비율을 HTML 리포트로 출력하는 도구로, 비디오 다운로드 없이 CPU만으로 동작합니다 [20].
- **NVIDIA Cosmos**: 자율주행 및 결함 이미지 생성 등 5가지 클라우드 네이티브 블루프린트를 Data Factory에 추가하고, 시뮬레이션 환경에서 자율주행 정책과 양팔 로봇 제어를 검증하는 Cosmos 3 Nano 모델 변형을 제공합니다 [79].
draft.section_devtools:
- **DeepInfer**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 모델을 지원하는 오픈소스 추론 프레임워크로, NVIDIA SM100 GPU 및 Huawei Ascend 950 NPU 지원과 함께 FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP 커널 및 비동기 스케줄링을 Apache 2.0 라이선스로 제공합니다 [42].
- **DeepSeek Search 및 Fetch API**: 구조화된 웹 검색 결과와 단일 웹페이지 마크다운 추출을 제공하는 API로, 토큰 수가 아닌 성공한 요청 1,000건당 0.75달러로 과금됩니다 [11].
- **Recursive Flint**: Apache 2.0 라이선스의 40B MoE 모델(토큰당 약 2.5B 활성화)로 262K 컨텍스트를 지원하며, RTX Spark, DGX Spark, GeForce RTX 등 로컬 하드웨어 실행에 최적화되었습니다 [62, 66].

- **Anthropic Agent Skills**: 벤더 중립성을 확보하기 위해 Agent Skills 표준을 리눅스 재단 산하 Agentic AI Foundation(AAIF)에 기증했습니다 [75].
